headline: Qatar repairs Ras Laffan, meets Iran acting oil minister
dek: Qatari Energy Minister Saad al-Kaabi met Iran's acting oil minister Hamid Bovard on energy cooperation; Qatar repairing Iranian-attack damage at Ras Laffan LPG plant that cut output. Chinese Premier Li Qiang told Iran's First VP Mohammad Reza Aref (SCO sidelines, Dushanbe) that…
sources: Reuters (Qatari energy ministry statement; Xinhua for Li Qiang meeting); Press TV (IRGC spokesman Mohebbi)
fault_line: Is China's dialogue push real peacemaking — or cover while Iran rebuilds?

sections.what_happened: Qatari Energy Minister Saad al-Kaabi met Iran's acting oil minister Hamid Bovard on energy cooperation; Qatar repairing Iranian-attack damage at Ras Laffan LPG plant that cut output. Chinese Premier Li Qiang told Iran's First VP Mohammad Reza Aref (SCO sidelines, Dushanbe) that sovereignty/security of all countries should be respected, urging peace, dialogue, negotiations. IRGC spokesman Mohebbi (Press TV): most US bases in Middle East 'rendered inactive', US forces exhausted; Iran's response to aggression 'much stronger'.
sections.what_verified: Reuters wire for both meetings; Xinhua for the China-Iran language.
sections.what_disputed: none on the meetings; Mohebbi's 'bases inactive' claim is Iranian military rhetoric, contradicted by CENTCOM's posture statements.
sections.why_matters: While Washington weighs the Mother of All Bombs, Beijing tells Tehran: sit down and talk. China keeps positioning itself as the adult in the room.
sections.context: Background: Gulf diplomacy track — UPDATE: Qatar repairs Ras Laffan, meets Iran acting oil minister; China urges Iran dialogue at SCO

totw_analysis: Our read: While Washington weighs the Mother of All Bombs, Beijing tells Tehran: sit down and talk. China keeps positioning itself as the adult in the room. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is China's dialogue push real peacemaking — or cover while Iran rebuilds?
